solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimmer is seen in a little water, say, with nothing on

indicators.note: with nothing on means the zero is attached after the rest
is seen in says the word is sits inside the little water

parts.note: a cubic centimetre, CC, is an example of a small quantity of liquid
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fish glimpsed in a tiny puddle with no cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks CC as just one example of a little water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cisco is a North American freshwater whitefish, so it is a kind of swimmer.

clue.text: Mystic scholar seen in taxi with top celebs?

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A mystic is spotted riding in a cab with famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabalist studies the Kabbalah, Jewish mystical teaching, so is a scholar of mysticism.

clue.text: Warehouse employee brought up as handle becomes weak

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
rots means decays, becomes weak

explanation.surface: A warehouse worker was raised to think a tool handle weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman is the person in charge of goods kept in a store or warehouse.

clue.text: For the solver, a piece of cake (the canapes sound revolting)

indicators.note: revolting says the letters of the fodder rise up and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A solver finds the clue easy, though the canapés sound disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' reads as disgusting but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a piece of cake is easy; this phrase describes a matter settled with no difficulty.

clue.text: Hurry with business lunch, then go back around end of afternoon

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
lunch is a meal

indicators.note: around says the turned word wraps round the letter that follows
go back says the word go is turned the other way round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: A busy worker grabs a working lunch, then heads back to the office late in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG, and 'around' puts N, the end of 'afternoon', inside it to give ONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Come along is an urging phrase telling someone to hurry up.

clue.text: A rail company motto: "every second counts"

indicators.note: every second picks alternate letters of motto, starting with its second

explanation.surface: A railway firm's slogan stresses that each moment matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' is the bird, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Coots belong to the rail family of birds, so a coot is an example of a rail.

clue.text: Reform overdue after fellow pulled the strings

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the word for fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: Reform says the letters of overdue are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A reform that was long delayed came after one man worked behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull the strings is to control events covertly, which is to have manoeuvred.

clue.text: Job seeker might show this past record of hard work?

indicators.note: past record of hard work means the record word follows the work word

parts.note: application is diligent effort, hard work
form is a record of past performance, as in a racehorse's form

explanation.surface: A jobseeker might show evidence of previous diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone applying for a job fills in and submits this document.

clue.text: One labouring principally in Middle Eastern territory?

definitions.text: One labouring principally in Middle Eastern territory?

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the country name

parts.note: Oman is a country in the Middle East
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: principally picks the first letter of labouring

explanation.surface: Describes a worker in the Gulf, likely in the petroleum industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working in petroleum is very likely labouring in a Gulf state such as Oman.

clue.text: Channel crossing's final part, say

parts.note: the final letter of crossing is G
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Swimming the Channel, the last stretch is the hardest, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel, but it is a drain for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel carrying rainwater, along a roof or the side of a road.

clue.text: Stopped working, being penniless and sad

parts.note: someone penniless is broke
feeling sad is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed in tears because they had no money and felt miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that has failed has ceased to function; the phrasal verb describes exactly that.

clue.text: TV programme shows very good French department

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for very good
the Lot is a département of south-west France

explanation.surface: A television show is praised as excellent and set in a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial episode made to test whether a television series will be commissioned.

clue.text: Very minor reverses in amateur play

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the word for amateur

parts.note: a lay person is a non-professional, an amateur

indicators.note: reverses says the word for very minor is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small, very minor

explanation.surface: A small-scale amateur dramatic production suffers setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' looks like a noun for setbacks but signals the turnaround; 'play' is the definition, slack, not a staged drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Play here means freedom of movement or slack, the sense of room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Unmarried priest given stick entering church

indicators.note: entering says the priest and stick go inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
a bat is a stick used in sport

explanation.surface: A single priest is handed a staff as he walks into church.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from marriage and sex is described as celibate; it's a near synonym.

clue.text: Politician in a flash becoming unreliable

indicators.note: in says the politician sits inside the word for a flash

parts.note: a flash is an instant
CON is short for a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician suddenly turns untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconstant is changeable and fickle, so cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Study noise of birds from Northern Europe

parts.note: to scan is to study closely
a din is a loud noise
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: Researching birdsong from the far north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandinavia covers Norway, Sweden and Denmark, lands in the north of Europe.

clue.text: Do we hurry up, touring old film studios?

indicators.note: touring says the turned letters go round the letter for old
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to nip is to hurry somewhere briefly

explanation.surface: A film crew asks if they must rush round an old set.
explanation.walkthrough: PINEWOOD Studios, west of London, is a British film studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinewood is the name of a famous complex of British film studios.

clue.text: Newly-trained 2 now working

indicators.note: Newly-trained says the letters of the cross-referenced word are put into new order

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer at 2 down, a warehouse worker

explanation.surface: A recently trained warehouse worker has started the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or project that is up and running has come into operation, now working.

clue.text: No practical sort, he rushed about, getting bright red reportedly

indicators.note: about says the word for rushed goes round he

parts.note: tore means rushed
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly says the colour word is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Titian is a bright auburn red, named after the Venetian painter

explanation.surface: An impractical man dashed around and went red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian red is a bright auburn named after the Venetian painter; 'reportedly' means only its sound is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist deals in ideas rather than practice, so is not a practical sort.

clue.text: Rogues sleep under canvas on board ship

indicators.note: on board says the word goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to camp is to sleep in a tent

explanation.surface: Villains bed down in tents aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous rascals, a mild synonym for rogues.

clue.text: Mostly cursed large weed

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word for cursed is dropped

parts.note: darned is a mild word for cursed

explanation.surface: A huge, largely damned weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Darnel is a ryegrass that grows as a weed among cereal crops.

clue.text: Charles when speaking secures wig

indicators.note: when speaking says the word for secures is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to secure something with a knot is to tie it

explanation.surface: Charles, while giving a speech, fastens down his hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wig' looks like a hairpiece but is the old verb to wig, to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To wig someone is to rebuke them severely, an old British use of the word.

clue.text: Commotion near centre of Preston, close to university

indicators.note: close to says the following letters sit right next to the letter for university
centre of picks the middle letters of Preston

explanation.surface: A disturbance breaks out near the middle of Preston, by the university.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is a town in Lancashire, England; its central letters are EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is agitation or disturbance among people, a near synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Guy is steady, regularly so

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of is steady, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A man is calm and dependable, consistently so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope or wire bracing a mast or tent, and so is a stay.

clue.text: Comic book craze I abandoned for good

indicators.note: abandoned for says the letter I is dropped and replaced by the letter for good

parts.note: a mania is a craze

explanation.surface: A reader gives up a passion for comic books for the sake of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Manga are Japanese comics, so a manga is a kind of comic book.

clue.text: Sports ground: area certain people set foot inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for set foot sits within the word for certain people

parts.note: some means certain people
trod means set foot

explanation.surface: A few people step onto a patch of a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astrodome in Houston was a famous domed stadium, a ground for sports events.

clue.text: Noticeably shrewd, admitting foreigner a short time later

indicators.note: admitting says the word for shrewd lets the other letters in

parts.note: sly means shrewd or crafty

indicators.note: later says the time letter comes after the word for foreigner

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner
T, short for time

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted person lets in an outsider after only a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something salient stands out, so doing it saliently means doing it prominently and visibly.

clue.text: Computer device rejected in some domiciles

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of computer kit is turned away from some homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is the hardware that links a computer to a phone or cable line.
